# Setting up

For grown-ups. Two minutes, once. Back to [[Today]].

> [!tip]- 1. Put it on your home screen
> - **iPhone:** open this page in Safari, tap Share, then **Add to Home Screen**.
> - **Android:** open it in Chrome, tap the menu (three dots), then **Install app**.
> - Or tap **More**, then **Put it on my home screen**.
>
> It works without internet once it has loaded.

> [!tip]- 2. How a week works
> Each week has one game, the same week as the grown-up class. **Today** shows it as cards, top to bottom.
> 1. **This week's game:** what you need and how to play. Tap **Open the lesson** for the whole page.
> 2. **Say it together:** one new line a day. Say the earlier lines too. Sunday is the whole game. **One line at a time** shows each line big, with the voice.
> 3. **Now you are the teacher:** swap. The kid asks the questions, and the grown-up gets one wrong on purpose.
> 4. **This week's words:** tap a word to hear it, then pick a color.
> 5. **Do the moves:** a gesture for each phrase.
>
> Weeks with no class keep last week's game.

> [!tip]- 3. The buttons
> They sit along the bottom of the screen.
> - **Today** (house): this week's game.
> - **Look up** (magnifying glass): any word in English or Greek.
> - **More** (three dots): Send homework, Share feedback, What's new, Put it on my home screen.
>
> Under the cards on Today: **Play Γιαγιά** (a word game with this week's words), **All lessons**, and **Look up a word**.

> [!tip]- 4. Colors
> Red is "not yet", yellow is "kind of", green is "got it". Tap the color after the kid tries the word from memory. Tap it again to clear it.

> [!tip]- 5. Updates and your work
> - Updates arrive by themselves in the background. Nothing to tap.
> - Colors, φόρα and notes live on this phone (or computer) only. It saves as you go and updates never touch it. On an iPhone, open it from the home screen icon: in a Safari tab, iPhones clear site data after about a week away.

notes.Games.md:
# Games

Back to [[Today]].

> [!summary]- Γιαγιά (find the notebooks, don't get fed)
> [Play Γιαγιά](obsidian://greekquent?open=giagia) (works offline)
> - Walk around the house and find 7 notebooks. Each one says a Greek word. Pick what it means.
> - Γιαγιά wants to feed you. If she catches you 3 times, it's dinner. Find all 7 and run out the door.
> - **Words from:** a kid lesson or all your words. On a word card, tap **More**, then **Play Γιαγιά with this word** to play that word and the words it goes with.
> - On a phone, use the arrows under the house or swipe. On a computer, use the arrow keys.

> [!summary]- Word web (tap, double-tap, hold)
> - Open a word card, tap **More**, then **Word web**.
> - Tap a word to hear it and move there. Double-tap a purple word to hear more than one. Hold a word to see what it goes with.

> [!summary]- Dessert word (a treat after the lesson)
> - At the bottom of [[Today]]. Pick a word, say it, make up a move, and draw it.
> - Tap **Add our own** to put your favorite words in the jar.

> [!summary]- Hello song
> - At the top of [[Today]]. Sing it together to start, and do the moves.
notes.What's New.md:
# What's new

Back to [[Today]].

> [!info]- November 18: Greekquent on the web
> - Greekquent now runs in the browser, on iPhone, Android and computers. Put it on your home screen from **More**.
> - Your work stays on your phone. **More**, then **Back up my work** saves a copy.
> - Updates arrive by themselves.

> [!info]- November 18, evening: small fixes
> - Word web: holding a word plays the phrase once (εγώ → Εγώ θέλω να πάω), without saying the word twice.
> - Your world shows on Today from the start, even before your first φόρα.

> [!info]- November 18, late night: tidier pages
> - Word pages: Hear it, Word web and More sit in one row, with the three colors below.
> - Hold a word in the Word web and you hear that word first, then it in a phrase.
> - The More menu is shorter. Ask on video is inside Ask.
> - Web app: your work saves as you go, so Back up and Check for updates are gone. Updates wait for a break instead of reloading while you work.

> [!info]- November 18, night: φόρα for almost everything
> - Comebacks, today's line and the rally now ask **Had it** or **Not yet** after you check. Had it counts like a word you got right. Not yet still earns 1 for trying.
> - Finishing a read-through, the rally swap, the hello song or a kid card (**We did it**) earns 2. Sending homework earns 3, and asking the class earns 2. Once a day each.
> - **Guess first** in Look up earns 1, and a new word in the **Word web** earns 1 (up to 5 a day). The Story Lines game counts too.
> - A small "+3 φόρα" shows at the top when points land.
> - Under the φόρα bars: "Your last 2 weeks. Today is blue."

> [!info]- November 18, after midnight: Word web card moved
> - When you hold a word in the **Word web**, its card now shows above the web, over the instructions. It no longer covers the other words.

> [!info]- November 18, midnight: Your world
> - The φόρα card now has a small world to grow. Pick one: a **Village** that grows from ancient to Byzantine to an island harbor to a modern city, an **Olive grove** from saplings to harvest to the press to a tasting, or a **Pet**, Φοράκι, that hatches and grows.
> - **Green words build it**, and it never shrinks. φόρα only sets the weather: a quiet night, an evening, a sunny day, or a festival.
> - Tap the picture to play it again and hear a word. The pet says your green words. Grown-ups: it grows with green words, so it never punishes a day off.
> - Change your world any time from **How φόρα works**. Nothing is lost.

> [!info]- November 18, night: φόρα, Story puzzle and a tour
> - **Πήρες φόρα;** Right answers in the games and the puzzle fill up the new card on Today. Say the answer out loud.
> - **Story puzzle:** under Say it together, build each line from word tiles. Drag them or tap them. A new line comes each day.
> - **The tour:** the first time, Today shows one tip at a time, games first. Take it again from More, then Take the tour.

> [!info]- November 18, late: Word web says μπορώ να βλέπω
> - When you hold a word in the **Word web**, it now uses the verb form you already know after να: μπορώ να βλέπω (I can see). Before, it said βλέπω μπορώ να δω.
> - The one-time form (μπορώ να δω) is shown in small letters under it, for when you are ready for it.

> [!info]- November 18, evening: Games from any word card
> - New **Games** page with Γιαγιά, the Word web, the dessert word and the hello song. Find it under **More**, then **Extras**, or tap **Games** on Today's More.
> - On a word card, **More** now has **Play Γιαγιά with this word**: you play that word and the words it goes with.

> [!info]- November 18: Double-tap for more than one
> - In the **Word web**, double-tap a purple word (a thing or a person) to hear more than one: το παιδί becomes τα παιδιά.

> [!info]- November 18: Γιαγιά arrows at your thumbs
> - In **Γιαγιά** on a phone, ◀ and ▲ are now at the bottom left for your left thumb, and ▼ and ▶ at the bottom right for your right thumb. The middle stays clear, so nothing covers them.

> [!info]- November 18: Hello song, εσύ fixed
> - In the hello song, the tune now goes up on σύ in εσύ, so the music stresses the same syllable you do.

> [!info]- November 17, late night: Hello song back to the first tune
> - **Sing the hello song** is back to the earlier tune, with the words lighting up in time.

> [!info]- November 17, night: The hello song is your teacher's tune
> - **Sing the hello song** now plays the melody your teacher sang, with his timing, as clean single notes.
> - The words light up as each one is sung. **Slower** stretches the whole song evenly.

> [!info]- November 17, late evening: Hello song back to the first tune
> - The new tune sounded rough partway through, so **Sing the hello song** is back to the earlier tune, with the words lighting up in time.

> [!info]- November 17, evening: The hello song is your teacher's tune
> - **Sing the hello song** now plays the melody your teacher sang, with his timing: the little scoops up into notes, the long held words, and the slow walk down on ελληνικά.
> - The words still light up right as each one is sung. **Slower** stretches the whole song evenly.

> [!info]- November 17, later: Hello song in time
> - The tune and the lit-up words now move together, all the way to the end. The last two lines are easier to sing: one word part on each beat.

> [!info]- November 17, night: A hello song
> - At the top of Today: a short Greek hello song with moves. Tap **Sing the hello song**: four ticks count you in, then each line lights up as you sing it.
> - **Slower** plays it slower. **Hear the words** says the words first, so you can learn them.
> - Sing it together at the start of practice. Doing it the same way every time tells everyone that Greek time has started.

> [!info]- November 17, late: One line at a time
> - On **Say it together**, tap **One line at a time**: each line opens big, with the voice, then all of them together. Close it with × or a tap outside.

**I eat** · say it: tróo

## Conjugation

When you meet it: now L13 · past was doing after Year One · did once έφαγα L23 · future να φάω L10

| Person | Now | Was doing / used to | Did (once) | Will |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| εγώ (I) | **τρώω** | **έτρωγα** | **έφαγα** | **θα φάω** |
| εσύ (you) | **τρως** | **έτρωγες** | **έφαγες** | **θα φας** |
| αυτός/ή/ό (he/she/it) | **τρώει** | **έτρωγε** | **έφαγε** | **θα φάει** |
| εμείς (we) | **τρώμε** | **τρώγαμε** | **φάγαμε** | **θα φάμε** |
| εσείς (you all) | **τρώτε** | **τρώγατε** | **φάγατε** | **θα φάτε** |
| αυτοί/ές/ά (they) | **τρώνε** | **έτρωγαν** | **έφαγαν** | **θα φάνε** |

Same "once" stem after να: Θέλω να φάω.

- **Who:** [[εγώ]] τρώω · [[εσύ]] τρως · [[αυτός]] τρώει · [[εμείς]] τρώμε · [[εσείς]] τρώτε · [[αυτοί]] τρώνε

- **How, when, where:** [[πολύ]] (a lot) · [[λίγο]] (a little) · [[γρήγορα]] (quickly) · [[τώρα]] (now) · [[μαζί]] (together) · [[έξω]] (out) · συνήθως (usually)

- **Little words:** [[και|τρώμε και πίνουμε]] (we eat and drink) · [[να|θέλω να φάω]] (I want to eat) · [[θα|θα φάμε μαζί]] (we'll eat together) · πρέπει να φάμε (we have to eat) · [[εμείς|εμείς τρώμε μαζί]] (we eat together) · [[κάτι|κάτι να φάμε]] (something to eat) · [[μαζί|τρώμε μαζί]] (we eat together) · ας φάμε (let's eat)

# Red eggs and candles

**The game:** Dye eggs red, or color paper ones, and decorate an Easter candle.

## Say it

- You: **Έχω ένα κόκκινο αυγό!** — I have a red egg!
- Grown-up: **Θέλεις κόκκινο αυγό;** — Do you want a red egg?
- You: **Ναι, θέλω!** — Yes, I do!
- You: **Έχω μια λαμπάδα.** — I have a candle.
- Ss: **Καλή Ανάσταση!** — Happy Resurrection! (said in Holy Week)

## You are the teacher

Swap: now you are the teacher. Ask the grown-up the questions.

- You (teacher): **Θέλεις κόκκινο αυγό;** — Do you want a red egg?
- Grown-up: answers, and sometimes gets it wrong on purpose. Catch it.
- You: **Όχι! Λάθος!** — No! Wrong!
- Grown-up: **Συγγνώμη!** — Sorry! (then says it right)
- You: **Μπράβο! Σωστά!** — Well done! That's right!

## Make it

The red eggs and the decorated candle.

## Do the moves

Do the move every time you say it.

- **Καλή Ανάσταση!**: Hold up an imaginary lit candle.
- **Καλό Πάσχα!**: Crack an imaginary red egg against a partner's.
- **Έχω μια λαμπάδα.**: Hold a tall candle and cup the flame.
- **Θέλεις κόκκινο αυγό;**: Offer a cupped red egg.

# Toy families

**The game:** Stuffed animals become a family, and you and the kid are another family, which lets you use the plural.

## Say it

- Grown-up: **Αυτή είναι η μητέρα. Αυτός είναι ο πατέρας.** — This is the mother. This is the father.
- Grown-up: **Έχουν δύο παιδιά.** — They have two kids.
- You: **Έχετε γάτα;** — Do you (all) have a cat?
- Grown-up (as toy family): **Ναι, έχουμε!** — Yes, we do!
- Grown-up: **Τι θέλουν τα παιδιά;** — What do the kids want?
- You: **Θέλουν νερό!** — They want water!
- You: **Μπορούμε;** — Can we?

## You are the teacher

Swap: now you are the teacher. Ask the grown-up the questions.

- You (teacher): **Έχετε γάτα;** — Do you (all) have a cat?
- You (teacher): **Τι θέλουν τα παιδιά;** — What do the kids want?
- You (teacher): **Μπορούμε;** — Can we?
- Grown-up: answers, and sometimes gets it wrong on purpose. Catch it.
- You: **Όχι! Λάθος!** — No! Wrong!
- Grown-up: **Συγγνώμη!** — Sorry! (then says it right)
- You: **Μπράβο! Σωστά!** — Well done! That's right!

## Make it

A handprint family tree: each person is a colored handprint with their Greek title written underneath.

## Do the moves

Do the move every time you say it.

- **Έχουμε δύο παιδιά.**: Circle hand between yourself and a partner ("we"), then show two short heights.
- **Έχετε παιδιά;**: Sweep a hand across the group, then show a child's height.
- **η γιαγιά μου**: Bend over a pretend cane, hand on your chest.
- **ο παππούς μου**: Twirl a pretend moustache, or play with κομπολόι worry beads.
- **Θέλουν…**: Point at two other people, then reach out eagerly.

# Where is Spider-Man?

**The game:** Your starter: move a toy around the table and chair, and the kid says where it is. Then he hides it and you have to find it.

## Say it

- Grown-up: **Πού είναι ο Spider-Man;** — Where is Spider-Man?
- You: **Ο Spider-Man είναι πάνω στο τραπέζι.** — Spider-Man is on the table.
- You: **Ο Spider-Man είναι κάτω από το τραπέζι.** — Spider-Man is under the table.
- You: **Ο Spider-Man είναι πάνω στην καρέκλα.** — Spider-Man is on the chair.
- You: **Ο Spider-Man είναι πάνω από την καρέκλα.** — Spider-Man is above the chair (in the air).
- You: **Είναι μέσα στο κουτί.** — He's in the box.
- You: **Είναι πίσω από την πόρτα.** — He's behind the door.
- You: **Είναι δίπλα στο βιβλίο.** — He's next to the book.
- Grown-up: **Δεν βλέπω τον Spider-Man! Πού είναι;** — I can't see Spider-Man! Where is he?
- You: **Δεν ξέρω!** — I don't know!
- Grown-up: **Εδώ είναι!** — Here he is!

**Pass him over:** one of you has Spider-Man, the other asks for him. Then swap.

- Grown-up: **Έχεις τον Spider-Man;** — Do you have Spider-Man?
- You: **Ναι, έχω τον Spider-Man!** — Yes, I have Spider-Man!
- You: **Ορίστε.** — Here you go.
- Grown-up: **Ευχαριστώ! Τώρα έχω τον Spider-Man!** — Thank you! Now I have Spider-Man!
- You: **Έχεις τον Spider-Man;** — Do you have Spider-Man?
- Grown-up: **Ναι, έχω τον Spider-Man. Ορίστε.** — Yes, I have Spider-Man. Here you go.
- You: **Ευχαριστώ!** — Thank you!

## You are the teacher

Swap: now you are the teacher. Ask the grown-up the questions.

- You (teacher): **Πού είναι ο Spider-Man;** — Where is Spider-Man?
- You (teacher): **Δεν βλέπω τον Spider-Man! Πού είναι;** — I can't see Spider-Man! Where is he?
- You (teacher): **Έχεις τον Spider-Man;** — Do you have Spider-Man?
- Grown-up: answers, and sometimes gets it wrong on purpose. Catch it.
- You: **Όχι! Λάθος!** — No! Wrong!
- Grown-up: **Συγγνώμη!** — Sorry! (then says it right)
- You: **Μπράβο! Σωστά!** — Well done! That's right!

## Make it

The kid draws a simple map of the room and sticks a small Spider-Man sticker wherever the toy was found.

## Do the moves

Do the move every time you say it.

- **Δεν έχω…**: Turn out empty pockets or open empty hands.
- **Πού είναι το κινητό μου;**: Pat your pockets, looking around.
- **Δεν βλέπω…**: Hand over your eyes, head turning.
- **Εδώ είναι!**: Point down hard at the spot and smile.
- **Γιατί δεν μπορείς;**: Both palms up, head tilted to the side.
- **Έχω δουλειά.**: Mime typing fast.
- **Μπορώ να δω;**: Point at your eye, then at the object, eyebrows up.
- **Πόσο κάνει;**: Rub thumb and fingers together.
- **Δύο ευρώ.**: Tap two fingers on the counter, one coin at a time.
- **Δεν ξέρω.**: Shrug with palms up.
- **Έχεις…;**: Hold out an open hand, palm up.
- **Έχω…**: Hug the toy to your chest.
- **Ορίστε.**: Hand the toy over with both hands.
- **Ευχαριστώ!**: Hand on your heart.

# Μπορείς; challenge

**The game:** Quick physical challenges. Easy ones get Ναι, μπορώ! and impossible ones get the keystone sentence.

## Say it

- Grown-up: **Μπορείς;** — Can you?
- You: **Ναι, μπορώ!** — Yes, I can!
- Grown-up: **Μπορεί!** — He can!
- You: **Θέλω, αλλά δεν μπορώ!** — I want to, but I can't!
- You: **Μπορώ;** — May I?
- Grown-up: **Ναι, βέβαια.** — Yes, of course.

## You are the teacher

Swap: now you are the teacher. Ask the grown-up the questions.

A sticker chart with a strong-arm picture at the top. One sticker per Μπορώ; he asks correctly.

- You (teacher): **Καλημέρα! Έχετε ντομάτες;** — Good morning! Do you have tomatoes?
- You (teacher): **Πόσο κάνουν;** — How much are they?
- Grown-up: answers, and sometimes gets it wrong on purpose. Catch it.
- You: **Όχι! Λάθος!** — No! Wrong!
- Grown-up: **Συγγνώμη!** — Sorry! (then says it right)
- You: **Μπράβο! Σωστά!** — Well done! That's right!

## Make it

Price tags with drawings of the food. The kid can write the numbers in Greek words once he knows them.

## Do the moves

Do the move every time you say it.

- **Πόσο κάνουν;**: Rub thumb and fingers together over the whole pile.
- **Έχετε ελιές;**: Pinch a small olive and pop it into your mouth.
- **Θέλω ένα κιλό.**: Weigh a heavy bag in one hand.
- **Ένα κιλό ντομάτες, παρακαλώ.**: Weigh the bag, then cup a round tomato.

# Traffic-light verb dice

**The game:** Roll a homemade die for the verb, then draw a color for the kind of sentence, using your red/yellow/green colors.

## Say it

- You (green): **Έχω καφέ.** — I have coffee.
- You (red): **Δεν θέλω ψωμί.** — I don't want bread.
- You (yellow): **Μπορείς αύριο;** — Can you tomorrow?
- You (yellow): **Βλέπεις τη θάλασσα;** — Do you see the sea?
- Grown-up: **Μπράβο!** — Well done!

## You are the teacher

Swap: now you are the teacher. Ask the grown-up the questions.

- You (teacher): **Μπορείς αύριο;** — Can you tomorrow?
- You (teacher): **Βλέπεις τη θάλασσα;** — Do you see the sea?
- Grown-up: answers, and sometimes gets it wrong on purpose. Catch it.
- You: **Όχι! Λάθος!** — No! Wrong!
- Grown-up: **Συγγνώμη!** — Sorry! (then says it right)
- You: **Μπράβο! Σωστά!** — Well done! That's right!

## Make it

Build the die together and let the kid draw the four pictures. The colors match the laminated packet, so the game teaches the system too.

## Do the moves

Do the move every time you say it.

- **Θέλεις έναν καφέ;**: Mime a tiny Greek coffee cup, little finger out.
- **Καλά, εσύ;**: Thumbs up, then a palm-up hand toward the partner.
- **Δεν έχω ώρα σήμερα.**: Tap your wrist, then shake your head.
- **Αύριο μπορείς;**: Roll a hand forward, then point at the partner.
- **Τέλεια!**: Kiss your fingertips.
- **Τα λέμε αύριο.**: Small fingers-together wave while rolling the hand forward.
- **Ξέρεις; – Δεν ξέρω.**: Tap your temple, then shrug.
- **στο καφενείο**: Mime moving a backgammon (τάβλι) piece on a board.
